Developer Profile

ABOUT XTREMERPIE

A self-taught developer passionate about building practical software, AI-powered systems, automation tools, and independent technology projects.

The Independent Mindset

I build software independently with a focus on practical utility and clean user sovereignty. Rather than building ephemeral toys or lock-in platforms, my projects are created to run directly on your hardware, respect your privacy, and solve real computing friction.

As a self-taught engineer, my knowledge is forged through continuous hands-on experimentation — breaking down operating system mechanics, investigating how browser engines manage tab memory, and connecting generative AI directly to local desktop automation pipelines.

Key Principles

Real Utilities FirstEvery application is built to solve a concrete everyday problem, not just as a visual mockup.
Zero Telemetry & User SovereigntyYour computer belongs to you. No tracking pixels, hidden analytics, or invasive data harvesting.
Craft & PerformanceOptimized memory footprint, responsive dark aesthetics, and attention to detail down to every millisecond.
Honest Independent BuildingNo fabricated claims, fake metrics, or venture capital bloat — genuine independent engineering.
Active Trajectory

Current Focus

  • Refining Xtreme AI Browser with local model integrations and tab sandboxing.
  • Advancing Rafail AI desktop orchestration framework.
  • Designing seamless cross-platform utilities in Python, Electron, and TypeScript.

Independent Goals

  • Build practical desktop software that operates independently of corporate walled gardens.
  • Integrate local intelligence and autonomous agent workflows into everyday productivity tools.
  • Maintain zero-telemetry and privacy-first foundations across every distributed application.
  • Continuously master software architecture, systems engineering, and modern web platforms.

Xtreme AI Browser v0.6.0 Released

Major release featuring the new Rafail AI sidebar copilot, multi-profile isolation compartments, and reduced memory footprint.
